newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Three candidates to stand for Mongolia president.
newsitem.headline: Three candidates to stand for Mongolia president.

text.p: Three candidates, including the incumbent, will stand in elections in May for Mongolia's president, Election Committee Chairman S. Lkhagvasuren said on Friday.

President P. Ochirbat, 55, will stand as candidate for the ruling Democratic Union Coalition in Mongolia's second direct presidential elections on May 19, when 1.2 million of Mongolia's 2.3 million people will be eligible to vote, the chairman said.
Ochirbat secured 57.8 percent of the vote in Mongolia's first direct presidential elections in June 1993.
He ran as candidate for the then-opposition democrats after being dumped by the ruling ex-communist Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party (MPRP).
The opposition MPRP would field its chairman and former speaker of parliament, N. Bagabandi, 47, as its candidate for the presidency, the election committee said.
The tiny Mongolian United Traditional Conservative Party, which has one seat in the Great Hural, or parliament, would field J. Gombojav, another Great Hural member, it said.

Gombojav resigned from the MPRP earlier this month, saying the former communist party was proving unable to change with the times. The move allowed him to contest the presidency for the Traditional Conservatives.
"I made this decision in the interests of the nation," he said. "I have to put the interests of the country above those of the party."
Each party with at least one member of parliament can field one candidate for the presidency.
The Democratic Union Coalition won a stunning 50 of the 76 seats in parliament in election last June to take power after 75 years of rule by Mongolia's communists and their heirs.
